_doc: Hand-written source for data/letters/memory-chain.json. No Hebrew here: the word comes from data/vocab/words.json by vocabId, the letter glyph from data/letters/letters.json. Build and verify with: node tools/letters/build_memory_chain.mjs [--check]

soundChecks._doc: soundClass -> regex the consonants.json english line must match (anchored). Used to prove each 'same' claim per tradition.

letters.line: Silent. It only holds a vowel, like the little pause in uh-oh.

picture.idea: A silent mime in a handstand. The handstand body is the letter.
picture.alt: Aleph becomes a silent mime doing a handstand

letters.story: A mime's silent handstand. Uh-oh! Father cheers: aba!
letters.tip: Silent twin: ayin is a curved cup with no crossing diagonal.
risk: Silent letter: the hook is a pause, not a consonant.
Ashkenazi: fully silent, no glottal stop (consonants.json).

letters.line: B like Ball (the dot inside is the ball). No dot: V.

picture.idea: A bungalow seen from the side with a ball inside; the floor sticks out at the back.
picture.alt: Bet becomes a bungalow with a ball inside

letters.story: A bungalow with a ball inside: B! Bayit is a house.
letters.tip: Not kaf: bet has sharp corners and its floor sticks out at the back.
risk: The chain teaches the dotted sound (b); the undotted v is shown only as the no-ball rule.

letters.line: Hard G like Grumpy, never a J sound.

picture.idea: A grumpy camel stomping forward, one foot kicked out ahead: the foot is gimel's foot.
picture.alt: Gimel becomes a grumpy camel stomping with one foot kicked out

letters.story: A grumpy camel stomps off: G! Gamal is a camel.
letters.tip: Not nun: gimel has a foot kicked out at the bottom left.
risk: Camel hooks can read as a regional stereotype; flagged earlier for reviewers (tools/review/questions.mjs).
Some Sephardi communities have a gh sound; consonants.json says hard g, so only that is claimed.

letters.line: D like Dive.

picture.idea: A diving board sticking out from one post over a pool.
picture.alt: Dalet becomes a diving board on one post over a pool

letters.story: Dive off the board: D! Delet is a door.
letters.tip: Not resh: dalet has a sharp corner; resh is one rounded curve.
risk: Sephardi: some communities say a soft d (consonants.json); not claimed here.

letters.line: H like Hut: just a breath. Silent at the very end of a word.

picture.idea: A small hut on a mountain with a gap in the left wall.
picture.alt: He becomes a small hut on a mountain with a gap in the wall

letters.story: A hut up on a mountain: hhh! Har is a mountain.
letters.tip: Not chet: he has a gap in the left wall; chet is closed.
risk: Final he without mappiq is silent; this chain uses a word-initial he.

letters.line: V like Vine. (It also writes the vowels o and u in other words.)

picture.idea: One straight vine hanging from a hook: the letter is the vine, the hook is the ceiling hook.
picture.alt: Vav becomes a single straight vine hanging from a hook

letters.story: A vine hangs from a hook: vvv! Vav means hook.
letters.tip: Not zayin: zayin has a bar on top; vav is a plain single stroke.
risk: The word is the letter's own name (vav, hook, rank 602). The older example, the rose, is rank 1694 and outside the 1500 limit.
Sephardi: some say a w sound (consonants.json); not claimed.

letters.line: Z like Zipper: zzzip.

picture.idea: A zipper pull on a zipper with gold teeth: a short bar on top and a straight stem down.
picture.alt: Zayin becomes a zipper pull on a zipper with gold teeth

letters.story: A gold zipper goes zzzip! Zahav means gold.
letters.tip: Not vav: zayin is short and has a bar across the top.
risk: The letter name is also slang in Israeli speech (flagged earlier for reviewers); the picture and hook stay clean.
consonants.json marks z as a standard value not in its fetched table.

letters.line: A scrape from the throat, like the ch in loch said the Scottish way. Not lock, not the ch of chair.

diff.sephardi: Strict Sephardi reading uses a deeper throat sound; the loch scrape is the common Israeli value.

picture.idea: A closed gate at the edge of a loch (a lake), with a jug of milk standing at the gate.
picture.alt: Chet becomes a closed gate beside a loch with a jug of milk

letters.story: A closed gate by the loch: chhh! A jug of milk, chalav.
letters.tip: Not he: chet is closed all round; he has a gap in the left wall.
risk: Many English speakers say loch as lock; teach the scrape, not the k.
No cat here: the one cat picture in the set is nun.
Sephardi differs: see perTradition.

letters.line: T like Tea.

picture.idea: A round teapot full of tea, its top curling inward.
picture.alt: Tet becomes a round teapot full of tea with its top curling in

letters.story: A teapot full of tea, then a telephone call: telefon.
letters.tip: Not mem or samekh: tet is one round bowl with a curl at the top.
risk: The word is a loanword (telefon), chosen for picturability; it is not drawn, the teapot is the hook.
consonants.json says it was not sourced which Sephardi or Mizrahi communities keep an emphatic tet; only plain t is claimed.

letters.line: Y like Yo-yo.

picture.idea: A tiny hand at the top of the line flicking a yo-yo on its string.
picture.alt: Yod becomes a tiny hand at the top flicking a yo-yo on a string

letters.story: A yo-yo bobs from your arm: Yo! Yad.
letters.tip: Not vav: yod is tiny and floats at the top.
risk: The vocabulary record glosses yad as arm; the picture shows the hand at its end (hand is the record's second sense).
Yod also writes the vowels i and ei in other words.

letters.line: K like Cup, with the dot inside. No dot: KH like loch.

picture.idea: A cup lying on its side: the C-shape is the letter.
picture.alt: Kaf becomes a cup lying on its side

letters.story: A cup, shaped like a cupped palm: kaf.
letters.tip: Not bet: kaf is one soft curve. Not pe: no curl inside.
risk: Gloss in the vocabulary is palm, paw; the cupped-palm sense ties to the cup.
Hook cup starts with the letter c but the sound k.
qof also says K: the kite picture keeps them apart.

letters.line: L like Lamp.

picture.idea: A tall lamp post with a bent arm reaching high, lighting the ground below.
picture.alt: Lamed becomes a tall bent lamp post with a cone of light

letters.story: A tall bent lamp shines: lechem means bread.
letters.tip: Only lamed rises above the line, so it is rarely confused.
risk: The vocabulary record is flagged for review (pointing source).

letters.line: M like Mailbox: mmm.

picture.idea: A mailbox on a post with a letter sticking out and a small flag.
picture.alt: Mem becomes a mailbox on a post with a letter and a flag

letters.story: A mailbox keeps letters safe from mayim, water.
letters.tip: Not final mem: open mem has a gap at the bottom left.
risk: The pointing of this vocabulary record came from the phrasebook and is not native-reviewed.

letters.line: N like Nap.

picture.idea: A cat curled up asleep, side view, with a Z for its snore. The only cat picture in the set.
picture.alt: Nun becomes a cat curled up asleep

letters.story: A cat takes a nap. Ner is a candle.
letters.tip: Not gimel: nun has a flat base and no kicked-out foot.
risk: This is the one cat picture in the set; the candle is only in the word, not drawn.
Keep the drawing clearly different from any other animal picture.

letters.line: S like Swim ring.

picture.idea: A striped swim ring floating on water: the closed ring is the letter.
picture.alt: Samekh becomes a striped swim ring floating on water

letters.story: A swim ring floats: sss! Sefer is a book.
letters.tip: Not final mem: samekh is round all over; final mem is a box.
risk: Sin (shin with the left dot) also says S; it is not one of the 27 forms here. See shin.

letters.line: Silent in Israel, like alef: you hear only the vowel.

diff.sephardi: Some Sephardi readers say a deep throat sound; do not try it in Israeli speech.

picture.idea: A big open eye: the sweeping lid curve is the letter.
picture.alt: Ayin becomes a big open eye whose lid curve is the letter

letters.story: A big eye blinks slowly: ayin means eye.
letters.tip: Not tsadi: ayin sweeps in one curve; tsadi has a flat base and a fork.
risk: The word is the letter's own name.
Sephardi differs: see perTradition.

letters.line: P like Pop, with the dot inside. No dot: F.

picture.idea: A wide-open mouth blowing one big bubble, the curl inside the letter being the tongue.
picture.alt: Pe becomes a mouth blowing a bubble with the tongue curled inside

letters.story: Pop! A mouth blows a bubble: peh.
letters.tip: Not kaf: pe has a curl tucked inside at the top left.
risk: The vocabulary record is flagged for review (pointing source).

letters.line: TS like the middle of pizza and the end of cats.

picture.idea: A slice of pizza with a bird perched on the pizza box; the leaning body is the letter.
picture.alt: Tsadi becomes a bird on a pizza box beside a slice of pizza

letters.story: A bird sits by a slice of pizza: tzipor.
letters.tip: Not ayin: tsadi has a flat base; its second stroke comes from the top right.
risk: No common English word starts with ts, so the hook sound is in the middle of pizza (not first).
Some traditional Sephardi communities say s (consonants.json); only ts is claimed.
The word is written tzipor in the vocabulary data and ts here for the letter.

letters.line: K like Kite: the same sound as kaf with a dot.

picture.idea: A red kite in the sky with its long string dangling below the line.
picture.alt: Qof becomes a red kite with a long string dangling below the line

letters.story: A kite flies on a long line: kav.
letters.tip: Not kaf: qof has a leg below the line. Same K sound.
risk: The older example, the monkey, is rank 1706 and outside the 1500 limit; kav (line) ties to the kite string.
Some Mizrahi communities say a deeper q (consonants.json); only k is claimed.

letters.line: A growl at the back of the throat. English R only spells the letter.

picture.idea: A smooth round head in profile, growling; no corners.
picture.alt: Resh becomes a smooth round head in profile, growling

letters.story: A round head growls rrr: rosh means head.
letters.tip: Not dalet: resh is one rounded curve; dalet has a sharp corner.
risk: The English R of round is not the Hebrew sound in any tradition: it is a spelling cue only (consonants.json).
The growl is Israeli; Sephardi is a rolled front r; Ashkenazi varies by region.

letters.line: SH like Shortcake, with the dot on the upper right. Dot on the left: S (sin).

picture.idea: A birthday shortcake with three candle flames: the three prongs are the letter.
picture.alt: Shin becomes a shortcake with three candle flames

letters.story: Three flames glow on a shortcake: sh! Shalom is peace.
letters.tip: Dot on the right says sh; dot on the left (sin) says s.
risk: Lithuanian Ashkenazi historically merged sh and s (consonants.json); not taught here.
The vocabulary record is flagged for review.

letters.line: T like Table (this word has the dot inside).

diff.ashkenazi: Ashkenazi reads tav WITHOUT the dot as s (Shabbos); this word has the dot, so it is t.

picture.idea: A small table with a baby beside it; the leg with a little foot is the letter.
picture.alt: Tav becomes a small table with a baby beside it

letters.story: A baby sits by a table: tinok.
letters.tip: Not he or chet: tav has a little foot at the bottom left.
risk: Undotted tav is s in Ashkenazi reading and th in some Sephardi communities (consonants.json); the chain teaches the dotted t only.
The vocabulary gloss is infant, baby (male).

letters.line: KH like the end of loch, same as kaf without a dot.

picture.idea: A king in a long robe whose cloak trails behind him into a loch (a lake).
picture.alt: Final kaf becomes a king whose long cloak trails into a loch

letters.story: A king's cloak trails into the loch: melekh, king.
letters.tip: Not dalet or resh: final kaf drops a tail below the line.
risk: Final forms end a word, so the word ENDS with the letter (cannot begin with it).
Many English speakers say loch as lock (the k of kaf with a dot): teach the scrape.
A dagesh in rare words makes it k (consonants.json).
The vocabulary record is flagged for review.

letters.line: M like Mom, same as mem.

picture.idea: A camping tent zipped shut beside the sea, with mom at the door.
picture.alt: Final mem becomes a zipped tent by the sea with mom at the door

letters.story: Mom zips the tent shut and swims in the sea: yam.
letters.tip: Not samekh: final mem is a hard box; samekh is round.
risk: Final forms end a word, so the word ENDS with the letter.

letters.line: N like Nail, same as nun.

picture.idea: One tall nail hammered upright into a big stone.
picture.alt: Final nun becomes one tall nail hammered upright into a stone

letters.story: Hammer a tall nail into a stone: even.
letters.tip: Not vav: final nun drops below the line.
risk: Final forms end a word, so the word ENDS with the letter.
The older example (garden, gan) is not in the vocabulary data; the nail is kept, the stone replaces the garden bed.

letters.line: F like Feather: same as pe with no dot.

picture.idea: A big feather held off the tip of a nose; the long stem is the tail of the letter.
picture.alt: Final pe becomes a big feather held off the tip of a nose

letters.story: Blow a feather off your nose: fff, af.
letters.tip: Not final tsadi: final pe has a round top with a curl inside.
risk: Final forms end a word, so the word ENDS with the letter.
The nose ties to the word af.

letters.line: TS like the end of nuts, same as tsadi.

picture.idea: A tall tree with Y-shaped branches and a long straight trunk, nuts hanging from the branches.
picture.alt: Final tsadi becomes a tall Y-branched tree with nuts hanging from it

letters.story: Nuts hang on the tall Y-branched tree: ts! Etz means tree.
letters.tip: Not final pe: final tsadi forks like a Y on top.
risk: Final forms end a word, so the word ENDS with the letter.
